        audition gain 1.6944275696653817 (peak 0.78), then gain 0.75

        The descending bells and the other effect/music volumes are unchanged.

Both source pages identified their licenses as Creative Commons 0 when
checked on 2026-11-12. Clips are bundled locally; playback makes no request
to Freesound. Click/error tones are generated by the game with Web Audio.

bgm-bossa.mp3 — selected C candidate (2026-11-12)
  Source: Short Elevator Music Loop by BlondPanda (Freesound sound 659889)
  https://freesound.org/people/BlondPanda/sounds/659889/
  License: CC0 1.0 Universal
  https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/
  Provider HQ MP3 preview: https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/659/659889_8927049-hq.mp3
  The bundled MP3 bytes are unchanged. Playback applies gain 0.6917813
  and 5 ms edge fades for a quiet loop boundary; the musical period is preserved.
  Plays locally; no external music request is made during the game.

Original result and answer feedback
  Result chimes/fanfare are synthesized in dist/effects.js.
  Answer cues in dist/feedback-audio.js layer locally synthesized ascending
  (correct) / descending (incorrect) bells with two quiet echo taps.
  The crowd plays behind these bells. Natural tails survive automatic screen
  swaps; explicit navigation, mute or a new guess fades them out over 120 ms.
  Mix: louder, longer bells lead the crowd by 120 ms. The crowd stays ducked
  during the cue and rises gently afterward.

Answer reveal accent
  Original glass shimmer synthesized by playRevealFeedback in
  dist/feedback-audio.js; no external recording is used.
  Plays once with the actual-price highlight (120 ms after the reveal starts),
  with a soft attack and natural release. It also marks a reveal after three
  misses, without implying a correct guess. Mute and manual navigation cancel it.

  The bundled full-length MP3 bytes are unchanged (220 seconds).
  Playback edits: gain 0.33892175462452356, matching the R3 audition;
  5 ms fades at loop edges, with a short fade when switching tracks.
  Title and final results use Wallpaper; questions and answer reveals use
  the existing Short Elevator Music Loop. Each track retains its position
  across screen changes, BGM mute and inactive tabs. All playback is local.
